items.iast:
sa vai puṁsāṁ paro dharmo
yato bhaktir adhokṣaje
ahaituky apratihatā
yayātmā suprasīdati
items.translation:
The supreme occupation [dharma] for all humanity is that by which
men can attain to loving devotional service unto the
transcendent Lord. Such devotional service must be unmotivated
and uninterrupted to completely satisfy the self.
items.essence: The highest dharma is unmotivated, uninterrupted bhakti — and the test of arrival is the self's complete satisfaction.
items.chanting_application:
Carry this verse into japa as a check: is today's chanting
unmotivated (ahaituki) — not for any return — and uninterrupted
(apratihatā) — not stopping when the mind protests? Where the
two qualities are present, satisfaction follows.

items.iast:
kṛte yad dhyāyato viṣṇuṁ
tretāyāṁ yajato makhaiḥ
dvāpare paricaryāyāṁ
kalau tad dhari-kīrtanāt
items.translation:
Whatever result was obtained in Satya-yuga by meditating on
Viṣṇu, in Tretā-yuga by performing sacrifices, and in
Dvāpara-yuga by serving the Lord's lotus feet can be obtained in
Kali-yuga simply by chanting the holy names of Hari.
items.essence: Four yugas, four prescribed methods — Kali's is the easiest, and yields the same result.
items.chanting_application:
You are doing in 16 rounds what a Satya-yuga sage attempted with
lifelong meditation. Approach today's japa with awe at the
efficiency, not with guilt that it seems too easy.

items.iast:
yat karoṣi yad aśnāsi
yaj juhoṣi dadāsi yat
yat tapasyasi kaunteya
tat kuruṣva mad-arpaṇam
items.translation:
O son of Kuntī, whatever you do, whatever you eat, whatever you
offer or give away, and whatever austerities you perform — do
that, O son of Kuntī, as an offering to Me.
items.essence: Every act, food, offering, austerity — re-pointed at Krishna, becomes bhakti.
items.chanting_application:
Begin each round this week with: "This round, Krishna, is for
You — not for my advancement, not for my peace, but as an
offering to You." A small intent shift; a large mood change.
items.source: Bhagavad-gītā As It Is, Chapter 9, Verse 27

items.iast:
man-manā bhava mad-bhakto
mad-yājī māṁ namaskuru
mām evaiṣyasi satyaṁ te
pratijāne priyo 'si me
items.translation:
Always think of Me, become My devotee, worship Me and offer your
homage unto Me. Thus you will come to Me without fail. I promise
you this because you are My very dear friend.
items.essence: Four instructions, one promise — Krishna gives His word.
items.chanting_application:
Krishna does not say "perhaps you will come." He says "you will
come to Me without fail" and adds "I promise." This week, when
doubt about the rounds arises, return to His pratijñā.
items.source: Bhagavad-gītā As It Is, Chapter 18, Verse 65

items.iast:
sarva-tyāga karileha 'nāmābhāsa' nahe nāśa
ārādhyo bhagavān vrajeśa-tanayaḥ
items.translation:
Even by leaving every other practice — if the chanting is left in
mere nāmābhāsa (shadow), it is not destroyed; nor is the
worshipable Lord, the son of the king of Vraja.
items.essence: Even the *shadow* of the Name does not perish — and the worshipable Lord remains the son of Nanda Mahārāja.
items.chanting_application:
When this week's chanting feels inattentive (nāmābhāsa), do not
conclude the day was wasted. Nothing about the Name is destroyed
by your inattention — only your benefit is delayed.
items.source: Caitanya Caritāmṛta, Madhya-līlā 8.275 (Mahāprabhu's instructions to Rāmānanda Rāya)

items.iast:
prabhu kahe, — 'vaiṣṇava-deha 'prākṛta' kabhu naya
'aprākṛta' deha bhaktera 'cid-ānanda-maya'
items.translation:
The Lord said: "A Vaiṣṇava's body is never material. It is a
spiritualized body, full of consciousness and bliss."
items.essence: Caitanya Mahāprabhu's verdict on the chanter's body — it is no longer prākṛta.
items.chanting_application:
Approach the body you sit in for japa not as an obstacle to
transcend but as already changing. The chanting itself is
spiritualizing it. Trust the process more than the sensations.

items.iast:
vāco vegaṁ manasaḥ krodha-vegaṁ
jihvā-vegam udaropastha-vegam
etān vegān yo viṣaheta dhīraḥ
sarvām apīmāṁ pṛthivīṁ sa śiṣyāt
items.translation:
A sober person who can tolerate the urge to speak, the mind's
demands, the actions of anger, and the urges of the tongue,
belly, and genitals is qualified to make disciples all over the
world.
items.essence: Rūpa Gosvāmī's six urges — controlling them is the qualification for spiritual leadership *and* for chanting.
items.chanting_application:
Before each round this week, take 5 seconds to notice: which of
the six urges (speech, mind, anger, tongue, belly, genitals) is
loudest in me now? Then offer that one to Krishna in the round.
items.source: Śrī Upadeśāmṛta (Nectar of Instruction) by Rūpa Gosvāmī, verse 1

items.iast:
tan-nāma-rūpa-caritādi-sukīrtanānu-
smṛtyoḥ krameṇa rasanā-manasī niyojya
tiṣṭhan vraje tad-anurāgi-janānugāmī
kālaṁ nayed akhilam ity upadeśa-sāram
items.translation:
The essence of all advice is that one should utilize one's full
time — twenty-four hours a day — in nicely chanting and
remembering the Lord's divine name, transcendental form,
qualities, and eternal pastimes, thereby gradually engaging
one's tongue and mind. In this way one should reside in Vraja
and serve Kṛṣṇa under the guidance of devotees.
items.essence: Engage the tongue (chanting) and the mind (remembrance) in the Name, form, qualities, pastimes — full-time.
items.chanting_application:
The instruction names the precise pair to engage: tongue + mind.
This week, after each round check: was the tongue engaged?
Probably. Was the mind engaged? Often less so. Bring the second
into alignment with the first.
items.source: Śrī Upadeśāmṛta (Nectar of Instruction) by Rūpa Gosvāmī, verse 8

items.iast:
nāmaikaṁ yasya vāci smaraṇa-patha-gataṁ
śrotra-mūlaṁ gataṁ vā
śuddhaṁ vāśuddha-varṇaṁ vyavahita-rahitaṁ
tārayaty eva satyam
items.translation:
If a devotee once utters the holy name of the Lord, or if it
penetrates his mind or enters his ear, that holy name will
certainly deliver him from material bondage — whether vibrated
properly or improperly, with correct or incorrect grammar, with
correct or incorrect pronunciation. O brāhmaṇa, the strength of
the holy name is therefore certainly great. But if one utters
the holy name in offense, it will not bring such effects.
items.essence: The Name delivers whether spoken purely or imperfectly — but offense blocks its full effect.
items.chanting_application:
Two warnings sit in this verse: do not despair over imperfect
pronunciation (the Name still works); and do not chant carelessly
enough to risk offense (the Name's full force is then blocked).
Mid-rounds, calibrate to both.
items.source: Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu by Rūpa Gosvāmī 1.2.234, cited in The Nectar of Devotion

items.iast:
ataḥ śrī-kṛṣṇa-nāmādi
na bhaved grāhyam indriyaiḥ
sevonmukhe hi jihvādau
svayam eva sphuraty adaḥ
items.translation:
No one can understand the transcendental nature of the name,
form, qualities, and pastimes of Śrī Kṛṣṇa through his
materially contaminated senses. Only when one becomes
spiritually saturated by transcendental service to the Lord do
the transcendental name, form, qualities, and pastimes of the
Lord become revealed.
items.essence: Material senses cannot grasp the Name. Only the service-tongue can taste it.
items.chanting_application:
You are not waiting to understand the Name and then chant. You
are chanting in service — and the Name reveals itself ON the
service-tongue. Sevonmukhe hi jihvādau. Begin with service mood;
the taste follows.
items.source: Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu by Rūpa Gosvāmī 1.2.234, cited extensively in NOD

items.iast:
oṁ pūrṇam adaḥ pūrṇam idaṁ
pūrṇāt pūrṇam udacyate
pūrṇasya pūrṇam ādāya
pūrṇam evāvaśiṣyate
items.translation:
The Personality of Godhead is perfect and complete, and because
He is completely perfect, all emanations from Him, such as this
phenomenal world, are perfectly equipped as complete wholes.
Whatever is produced of the complete whole is also complete in
itself. Because He is the Complete Whole, even though so many
complete units emanate from Him, He remains the complete balance.
items.essence: The Lord is complete. His emanation is complete. His chanting is complete. Wholeness is the only true unit.
items.chanting_application:
When today's chanting feels partial, return to pūrṇa. Krishna is
not missing anything from your distracted round. He is complete,
and the Name He IS is complete. Take shelter of the wholeness
that surrounds even your incompleteness.

items.iast:
hiraṇmayena pātreṇa
satyasyāpihitaṁ mukham
tat tvaṁ pūṣann apāvṛṇu
satya-dharmāya dṛṣṭaye
items.translation:
O my Lord, sustainer of all that lives, Your real face is
covered by Your dazzling effulgence. Kindly remove that
covering and exhibit Yourself to Your pure devotee.
items.essence: The petition of the upaniṣad — uncover Your face for the one who serves truth.
items.chanting_application:
Chant this week with the petition in mind: I am not asking for a
breakthrough, only for the brahmajyoti covering to part enough
that the face appears. The chanting is the asking.
